items.headline: Bessent Says Nvidia Needs ‘Dramatic Shakeup’ With Huang Out
items.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that Nvidia Corp. needs a “dramatic shakeup” in leadership after the ouster of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

items.headline: House Chairman Says Huang Agrees to Testify But No Date Set Yet
items.excerpt: Ousted Nvidia Corp. chief executive officer Jensen Huang agreed to testify before lawmakers behind closed doors on his relationship with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, according to Republican Representative John Moolenaar.

items.headline: VC Firm Run by Madonna’s Manager Has $7 Billion Anthropic Stake
items.excerpt: Dario Amodei was arguably one of the least famous people in the Beverly Hills home he visited in 2023. The Anthropic PBC chief executive officer sat across from actor-turned-venture capitalist Ashton Kutcher, and Guy Oseary, the legendary music manager and industry broker who owned the house.

items.headline: Peloton Tread Flex Lowers Entry Price for Home Treadmills to $2,195
items.excerpt: Peloton Interactive Inc.’s $2,195 Tread Flex is its least expensive treadmill to date, putting the brand within reach of more casual runners —including people who don’t usually enjoy running indoors.

items.headline: Apple Siri AI App Integrations Power Smart Glasses, iPhone Duo 2 Face ID Plan
items.excerpt: Also: A look at the race to bring Face ID to the iPhone Duo.

items.headline: Nvidia Sought Taipei’s Help Over Employee’s Chip Smuggling Case
items.excerpt: Nvidia Corp. appealed to Taiwanese officials after prosecutors on the island accused an employee of helping to smuggle AI chips into China, raising fresh questions about how the firm views its own role in stopping the illicit trade.

items.headline: AI Investors Brace for Data Center Restrictions
items.excerpt: PIMCO market strategist Tony Crescenzi is on Bloomberg This Weekend to assess what growing political resistance to data centers could mean for the AI investment boom, arguing that new restrictions may slow construction without derailing the broader buildout. items.headline: Wingtech to Challenge Dutch Court’s Nexperia Interim Order
items.excerpt: Wingtech Technology Co. said it opposes a Dutch court’s latest interim order in the dispute over Nexperia and plans to appeal, arguing the ruling lacks a factual basis and contains fundamental legal flaws, according to a stock exchange filing on Sunday.

items.headline: China’s Yoozoo Gets $214 Million Flash-Memory Components Order
items.excerpt: Chinese game developer Yoozoo Interactive Co. said one of its units received a 1.43 billion yuan ($214 million) order for flash-memory components, though it expects little impact on revenue or its financial data.

items.headline: Firmus Plans to Raise $3 Billion After IPO Collapse, AFR Says
items.excerpt: Firmus Grid Ltd. is planning a $3 billion private fundraising effort that will include new equity and debt issuance, as well as locking in pre-payments from customers including its backer Nvidia Corp. and Meta Platforms Inc., the Australian Financial Review reported.

items.headline: Korea’s Top Scorer in Tax Accountant Exam Admits to AI Cheating
items.excerpt: South Korea’s top scorer in national tax accountant qualification exams admitted that he used generative artificial intelligence and electronic devices to cheat in the tests, and has turned himself in to police.

items.headline: Carney, Lula Forge Closer Ties With Forests Funding, Visits
items.excerpt: Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney and Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva signaled closer ties on Sunday with funding to protect the world’s tropical forests and visits to each others’ countries.

items.headline: India Stock Market Rebounds as AI Trade Unwinds, Foreign Funds Return
items.excerpt: Indian stocks suffered bruising losses in the first nine months of the year as the artificial intelligence trade hoovered up global investor capital. The unwinding of that strategy has turned the Asian nation’s equities into world beaters.

items.headline: My Husband and His Chatbot
items.excerpt: What happens when an AI chatbot becomes the third person in a marriage? Morgan Meaker looks at whether algorithms are replacing the human friction real intimacy needs to survive. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Access to Users’ Photos
items.excerpt: The Italian Data Protection Authority fined Meta Platforms Inc. €805 million ($887 million) for accessing photos and videos of Android users’ galleries without their explicit consent.
